title: Libby PI recommendation row
description: Final ranked recommendations synthesized by the PI agent.

access_route.description: How this patient could practically reach the therapy today, copied from `accessibility.jsonl::access_status` (first/primary path when a row carries several). Under the unified-table contract EVERY therapy with any evidence gets a ranked row, including standard-of-care ones, so this field -- not the therapy's absence -- is what tells a reader an option is already approved care rather than experimental. Optional for backwards compatibility: cases ranked before the unified-table change omit it, and its presence on any row is what opts a case into the standard-of-care coverage gate in check_pipeline.py.

likelihood_of_effect.description: ≤ 25-word qualitative narrative for the at-a-glance ranked-prioritization table. Lead with a tier descriptor ('High in <subset>', 'Moderate', 'Low for <endpoint>') + the load-bearing evidence anchor (effect size, concordance across replicate trials, or trial reference). Distilled from the per-rank 'Likelihood of desired effect' prose.

toxicity_burden.description: Patient-level AE burden as a tier ('Low' | 'Moderate' | 'High') + parenthetical of 2-4 characteristic G3+ AEs. Aggregation rule: Low if all G≥3 rates < 20%, Moderate if any 20-50%, High if any > 50% or if treatment-related death > 0. Distinct from `counter_productive_moa` (col 5) which is mechanism-level risk.

description.description: ≤ 20 words. Names the mechanism-level risk that could blunt the therapeutic goal — T-cell exhaustion, antigen-loss escape, anti-angiogenic wound-healing impairment, etc. Distinct from patient AEs (those go in `toxicity_burden`).

counter_productive_moa.description: Mechanism-level counter-productive risk. Severity rule: Low if dissent is preference-flavored only, Moderate if a board persona dissented on mechanism grounds, High if a veto stood on mechanism grounds. Workup / diagnostic rows always `N/A`.

overall.description: ≤ 30-word declarative summary, rendered bold. Names the load-bearing tradeoff or scope — NOT the rank ordering. Sharpened from the per-rank 'Why this rank' prose. Examples: 'Strongest replicated 2L+ osteosarcoma RCT evidence; biomarker-independent backbone regardless of IHC.', 'The only DLL3-directed option when IHC is positive — preference-aligned but cross-tumor translation untested.'

surfaced_reason.description: Why a feature-targeting investigational intervention is surfaced in the Experimental table but not ranked as a live top-tier option. `none` (default) is a normally-ranked/assessed row (its recommend-strength lives in `status`). `unavailable` = the program is discontinued/terminated with no successor. `consolidated` = one of several products of an approach that is ranked once at the approach level (this row points to the approach). `thin_evidence` = no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy yet (e.g. tool-compound / gated). `not_enrollable` = cross-tumor mechanism evidence or geographically-inaccessible, informational only. The renderer groups and flags rows by this field; `status` remains the recommend-strength axis. Approved feature-targeting drugs are NOT surfaced here — they live in the Standard-of-care table.

scenario.description: Three values: `null` for biomarker-independent recs (default), the literal `"shared"` for the rank-1 workup row that gates whether biomarker-conditional recs apply, or `"<biomarker_short>:positive"` for recs that are valid only if the named biomarker confirms positive (e.g. `dll3_ihc:positive`). The negative branch is no longer emitted: if the confirmatory test is negative, biomarker-conditional recs are foreclosed and the cross-cutting caveat in `index.md` documents the foreclosure mapping.

scenario_label.description: Human-readable label for a `:positive` scenario, used inline in rendered docs (e.g. 'If DLL3 IHC ≥1% (preferably ≥25%)'). Null for `shared` workup rows and `null`-scenario rows.

targets.description: Snake-case identifiers for the targetable features this intervention acts on. Drives per-target grouping in the Recommendations table HTML. First entry is the primary target. Keys mirror the user-stated `profile.json::targetable_features[].feature` (snake-cased), e.g. `["kras_g12r"]`, `["cdkn2a_loss"]`, `["kras_g12r", "cdkn2a_loss"]` for a dual-target combination. For biomarker-gated cases the `scenario` field carries the same grouping signal; `targets[]` is the canonical source for non-gated cases.
